facts.fact: The World Bank appraisal document states that the CityWeb software has been deployed in 105 civil status centers 'to enable real-time monitoring and improve interoperability', with plans to expand nationwide; it gives no total of centers and no date, so the date is the document's.
The World Bank appraisal document states that obtaining a birth certificate can take days or weeks 'because the registry is still on paper'; no date is given, so the date is the document's.

The World Bank appraisal document states that Côte d'Ivoire lacks a comprehensive, nationwide electronic civil registry system, that paper records are stored locally with no centralized backup, and that the Ministry of Digital Transition confirmed the services to be digitalized, electronic civil registry services among them, are not currently active in the programme's selected areas; no date is given, so the date is the document's.

The World Bank's RAPID-CI Phase 1 credit (US$150m, appraised 18 September 2025) is to finance renovation, hardware, IT equipment, technical assistance and capacity building for digitizing and archiving civil registration data 'for the effective implementation of the CityWeb software', and to coordinate with an EU-funded project implemented by CIVIPOL on town hall connectivity and the digitalization and archiving of civil registries.
